title: WIPO IP Moot Court Competition 2027
overview: An international moot court competition on intellectual property law for teams of two law students (aged 35 or under) from the same university, with an optional coach. Teams are selected through a short video application; selected teams write memorials and argue online, and the top eight teams go to the finals in Geneva on 8 to 10 June 2027. Conducted entirely in English.
country: Switzerland (finals); written and online rounds from the home university
program_dates: Teams announced 30 November 2026; moot problem released 10 December 2026; written submissions due 1 February 2027; online rounds 1 to 12 March 2027; finals in Geneva 8 to 10 June 2027 (tentative timeline on the WIPO page)
deadline_text: Application period 12 October to 6 November 2026 (WIPO competition page, read 26 October 2026). WIPO: "All times are given in Geneva time (GMT+1)"; no closing hour is stated. FAQ: "Applications must be submitted by November 6, 2026."
deadline_timezone: Geneva time (CET, GMT+1); no closing hour stated
funding_details: WIPO FAQ: "WIPO will provide funding for the eight teams that qualify for the final rounds in Geneva, Switzerland. The funding covers the cost of travel, accommodation, and visa fees. Note that team coaches will not be funded by WIPO."
WIPO FAQ: "any additional cost associated with obtaining the visa must be borne by the participants."
WIPO FAQ: "No, there is no registration fee."
Teams that are not among the eight finalists take part in the written and online rounds only; no funding is mentioned for them.
age_requirement: Team members must be "aged 35 years or under at the time of application" (the limit does not apply to the coach)
experience_requirement: No work experience required; students must not have been admitted to practise law in any jurisdiction
education_requirement: Enrolled full-time or part-time in a law programme leading to a legal degree at the time of application (students who finished coursework but have not graduated are eligible; PhD students and students holding an LLB/LLM enrolled in another law programme are eligible)
nationality_requirements: No nationality condition stated in the 2027 Rules or FAQ
language_requirement: "The competition will be conducted entirely in English." The application video must be in English.
eligibility: Teams of two law students from the same university, plus an optional coach (a student or faculty member of the same university)
Each student aged 35 or under at the time of application
Enrolled in a law programme and not admitted to practise in any jurisdiction
Team authorised by the university (Dean of Law or faculty representative signs the declaration form)
Up to two teams per university; past winners are not eligible
other_requirements: Up to two teams from the same university may apply
documents_required: Declaration form signed by both students, the coach (if any) and the Dean or faculty representative
Pre-recorded video argument in English, maximum 5 minutes, answering one of the two questions in the Application Guidelines; both students must speak
application_process: Read the Application Guidelines, Competition Rules and FAQ on the WIPO page
Have the declaration form signed, complete the online application form and upload the video through the link on the WIPO page by 6 November 2026
Selected teams are announced on 30 November 2026

English only

benefits: Awards for winner, runner-up, best memorials and best oralists (no cash amounts stated)
action: Read the WIPO Application Guidelines and Rules, then submit the form, signed declaration and video before 6 November 2026 (Geneva time) if your law faculty authorises a team.
notes: The 2026 edition ran with a 6 October to 15 December 2025 application window; the competition repeats yearly.

title: Orange Corners RDC: 10-month programme for young entrepreneurs (Kinshasa and online)

overview: A free 10-month incubation programme for young Congolese aged 18 to 35 with an innovative business idea, concept or MVP in food security, environment and climate, water, green energy, local processing of minerals or digitalisation. It offers training, bi-weekly mentoring, networking, help finding funding (no direct funding) and free coworking space; in person in Kinshasa and online elsewhere in the DRC.
